newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to act properly against forex swings - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to act properly against forex swings - MOF.

text.p: Japan will continue to deal with excessive currency movements in the proper fashion, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.
"An excessively weak or strong yen is not favourable for the Japanese economy," he said.
Mitsuzuka said that stable currency moves were needed for the Japanese economy.
"We want exchange rates to stabilise," he told the news conference.
Japan will keep a close watch on currency movements, he added.
"We will continue to act properly against excessive currency moves," Mitsuzuka said.
Mitsuzuka added that confidence would likely return to the financial markets once the government starts carrying out detailed measures, such as revising laws, in order to implement various reforms.

The finance minister said the government would like to hold a meeting of experts to discuss future fiscal reforms after Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto returns from a Southeast Asian trip on January 14 and before January 20 when a parliamentary session starts.

The meeting will hammer out basic policies for forming the state budget for the fiscal year starting in April 1998 and will also set a timetable for achieving numerical targets for reducing the state deficit.
In December, the cabinet approved a proposal by a government advisory panel to cut the annual fiscal deficit to below three percent of gross domestic product by 2005.
